query: For additively manufactured high-entropy-alloy components, what single intervention could improve dimensional precision and mechanical integrity while reducing fabrication-induced defects? Formulate one hypothesis that identifies the intervention, explains its mechanism, predicts the improvement relative to the current fabrication baseline, defines the processing and application conditions under which it should hold, identifies supporting prior evidence, and proposes an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Post-process deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) of additively manufactured high-entropy alloys can reduce residual stresses and promote beneficial microstructural phase transitions, leading to improved dimensional precision and enhanced mechanical integrity with fewer defects.
generation.material_initial_state: High-entropy alloy components produced by laser melting deposition (LMD) that exhibit residual stress, thermal gradients, and fabrication-induced defects.
generation.intervention: Deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) applied after LMD fabrication.
generation.conditions: Apply DCT by immersing LMD-fabricated samples in liquid nitrogen (approximately -196°C) for an optimized duration (e.g., 24–48 hours) post-deposition under ambient pressure.
generation.structural_mediator: Reduction in internal residual stresses and induced phase transitions that refine the microstructure and increase lattice distortion.
generation.mechanism: The DCT process promotes uniform thermal contraction and accelerates induced phase transformations, which relieve internal stresses and reduce defect formation. This leads to improved dimensional stability and mechanical properties through a more homogeneous microstructure.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the as-deposited baseline, DCT-treated samples will show improved dimensional accuracy, enhanced tensile strength (roughly up to 11–25% improvement based on similar HEA systems), and reduced fabrication-induced porosity and defects.
generation.baseline: As-deposited high-entropy alloy components fabricated by LMD without any post-processing treatment.
generation.boundary: The intervention is expected to be effective for HEAs with a BCC structure processed by LMD; results may vary with different alloy systems, processing parameters, or if DCT conditions are not precisely controlled (e.g., significantly shorter or longer soak times).
generation.uncertainty: While evidence supports benefits of DCT in similar systems, the precise magnitude of improvement in dimensional precision and mechanical integrity in various high-entropy alloys remains to be fully quantified and may depend on specific alloy compositions and processing settings.

falsification_experiment.design: Fabricate two sets of HEA components using LMD. Subject one set to DCT (immersed in liquid nitrogen for 24–48 hours) and keep the other set as a control. Evaluate and compare both groups using standardized tests.
measurements: Dimensional accuracy using coordinate measuring machines (CMM) or laser scanning profilometry
Residual stress levels via X-ray diffraction (XRD) or hole-drilling method
Mechanical properties through tensile testing (measuring tensile strength and elongation)
Defect identification via micro-computed tomography (micro-CT) imaging
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the DCT-treated samples do not demonstrate statistically significant improvements in dimensional precision and mechanical integrity (tensile properties) or show no reduction in defect density compared to the as-deposited control, the hypothesis will be falsified.

## Abstract
AbstractHfNbTaTiZr high-entropy alloy has wide application prospects as a biomedical material, and the use of laser additive manufacturing can solve the forming problems faced by the alloy. In view of the characteristics of the one-time forming of additive manufacturing methods, it is necessary to develop non-mechanical processing modification methods. In this paper, deep cryogenic treatment (DCT) is first applied to the modification of a HEA with BCC structure, then the post-processing method of DCT is combined with laser melting deposition (LMD) technology to successfully realize the coordinated improvement of forming and strength–ductility synergistic improvement in lightweight Hf0.25NbTa0.25TiZr alloy. The final tensile strength of the alloy after DCT treatment is 25% higher than that of the as-cast alloy and 11% higher than that of the as-deposited alloy, and the elongation is increased by 48% and 10%, respectively. In addition, DCT also achieves induced phase transition without additional deformation.Keywords: laser melting deposition, high entropy alloy, deep cryogenic treatment, 3D printing, defects, strength–ductility synergistic improvement
## 1. Introduction

At present, the casting forming of HEAs is facing some problems due to their high melt viscosity, and laser additive manufacturing (AM) technology can effectively solve this problem [,,]. Laser melting deposition (LMD) technology has high energy density and complex-shape-forming ability, which can solve the problem of HEA forming and accumulate thermal stress in as-deposited alloy samples [].
